claims.text: High-temperature sliding wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu coating is governed by formation of a protective Cr2O3 layer.
Microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding of a FeNiCrCoCu coating is governed by formation of a protective Cr2O3 layer.
Increasing chromium by 10–20% relative to the baseline promotes enhanced oxide-layer formation.
Increasing the relative chromium content enhances the stability of the protective chromium oxide layer.
The relevant structural mediator is a continuous Cr2O3 layer at the sliding interface.
At elevated temperature, increased chromium accelerates development of a stable Cr2O3 film during sliding.
The Cr2O3 film acts as a physical barrier that impedes dislocation motion.
The Cr2O3 film impedes grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding reduce plastic deformation during sliding.
The chromium-enriched coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating.
The chromium-enriched coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation than the baseline coating.
The predicted effects apply around 500°C under controlled load in an oxidizing environment.
The coating may behave differently at lower temperatures or under non-oxidizing conditions.
